dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001

dependency_coverage.meaning: The third field of a system, a function u : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008

binders: Universally quantified real constants K = bulkModulus and ρ = density; these are implicit Lean parameters and do not vary with x or t.
A universally quantified system : LocalDef001 K ρ, supplying p,u : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ and the conditions described below.
Proof arguments for K > 0 and ρ > 0.
Universally quantified real coordinates x and t, with x the first function argument and t the second.

Within the system condition, for every x,t there exist real witnesses p_t,p_x,u_t,u_x. These witnesses may depend on the system and the point and are required to satisfy all four derivative assertions and both equations simultaneously.

Within each transport conjunct at each x,t there exist real witnesses for that function's time and space derivatives. The two conjuncts have separate existential witnesses, which may depend on K, ρ, the system and x,t.
hypotheses: The system carries ρ ≠ 0, already implied by ρ > 0.
The functions p and u are defined on all of ℝ × ℝ.
For every real x,t, the ordinary derivatives of τ ↦ p(x,τ) at t, ξ ↦ p(ξ,t) at x, τ ↦ u(x,τ) at t and ξ ↦ u(ξ,t) at x exist.
At every real x,t, those derivatives satisfy p_t(x,t) + K u_x(x,t) = 0 and u_t(x,t) + ρ⁻¹ p_x(x,t) = 0.
conclusions: Let c = √(K/ρ) and w₊(x,t) = p(x,t) + (ρc)u(x,t). For every real x,t there exist a₊,b₊ ∈ ℝ such that τ ↦ w₊(x,τ) has derivative a₊ at t, ξ ↦ w₊(ξ,t) has derivative b₊ at x, and a₊ + c b₊ = 0.

Let w₋(x,t) = p(x,t) − (ρc)u(x,t), with the same positive c. At the same arbitrary real x,t there exist a₋,b₋ ∈ ℝ such that τ ↦ w₋(x,τ) has derivative a₋ at t, ξ ↦ w₋(ξ,t) has derivative b₋ at x, and a₋ + (−c)b₋ = 0.
Both conclusions hold together at every point; equivalently, (w₊)_t + c(w₊)_x = 0 and (w₋)_t − c(w₋)_x = 0 everywhere, with existence of all displayed slice derivatives included.
mathematical_definitions: All arithmetic takes place in the standard real field, and derivatives use the usual topology defined by distance |a − b|.
For f : ℝ → ℝ, having derivative d at a means the ordinary two-sided derivative exists and equals d; equivalently, lim as h → 0 with h ≠ 0 of (f(a+h) − f(a))/h is d.
For q : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ, the time derivative at (x,t) differentiates τ ↦ q(x,τ) at t, while the space derivative differentiates ξ ↦ q(ξ,t) at x.
The transport predicate for q and constant speed s at (x,t) means that both slice derivatives exist and q_t(x,t) + s q_x(x,t) = 0.
Real.sqrt is the nonnegative square root of the nonnegative part of its input. Since K and ρ are positive, c = √(K/ρ) is strictly positive and satisfies c² = K/ρ.
The coefficient in both transformed functions is ρc. The second function uses this positive c inside p − (ρc)u and separately uses −c as its transport speed.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every pair of positive real constants K and ρ and every system consisting of real-valued functions p and u on all real space and time, with both coordinate slice derivatives existing everywhere and satisfying p_t + K u_x = 0 and u_t + ρ⁻¹ p_x = 0 everywhere, set c = √(K/ρ). Then the functions w₊ = p + ρc u and w₋ = p − ρc u both have time and space slice derivatives at every point, and they satisfy respectively (w₊)_t + c(w₊)_x = 0 and (w₋)_t − c(w₋)_x = 0 at every real space-time point.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The constants K and ρ must each be strictly positive. Cases with a zero or negative parameter have no substantive conclusion under these hypotheses, even though Lean's real inverse and square root are total operations.
The system additionally contains a nonzero-density condition; density zero is excluded before the positive-density hypothesis is used.
Both coordinates range over the entire real line, including negative times. There is no spatial interval, boundary, time half-line or restricted domain.

Differentiability is required separately in each coordinate at every point. Joint differentiability, continuity of the partial derivatives, second derivatives and any specified C¹ or C² regularity are not encoded as hypotheses or conclusions.

The target states pointwise first-order transport equations. It does not explicitly assert characteristic-curve constancy, a traveling-profile representation, initial-value formulas, existence or uniqueness of solutions, boundary conditions or a converse reconstruction theorem.

The symbols pressure, velocity, bulkModulus and density are mathematical roles for functions and constants; no physical units, constitutive interpretation, sign condition on p or u, or additional physical law is encoded.

Existential derivative witnesses lie inside the pointwise quantifiers. No globally specified derivative functions, regularity of their dependence on the point, or common witnesses for the two transformed functions are asserted.

There is no inherent empty-system vacuity for positive K and ρ: constant p and u have zero slice derivatives and satisfy the constructor's equations. The theorem itself quantifies over supplied systems and does not assert their existence.
